biological.citation: SPTAN1/NUMB axis senses cell density to restrain cell growth and oncogenesis through Hippo signaling. (PMID: 37843276)
biological.summary: High cell density induces phosphorylation of SPTAN1, which recruits NUMB1/2 to the plasma membrane, sequestering MARK kinases and enabling MST1/2 activation and downstream Hippo/YAP signaling to inhibit cell growth. Low cell density leads to SPTAN1 dephosphorylation, NUMB cytoplasmic relocalization, MST1/2 inhibition, and YAP activation. NUMB isoforms 3/4, unable to interact with phosphorylated SPTAN1, are selectively upregulated in liver cancer correlating with YAP activation.

biological.citation: ASHG 2010 - Dominant negative mutations in α-II spectrin cause early onset West syndrome with severe cerebral hypomyelination, spastic quadriplegia, and developmental delay. (H. Saitsu et al.)
biological.summary: In-frame mutations in SPTAN1 at the α/β spectrin heterodimer nucleation site produced thermolabile α-II(mut)/β-II spectrin heterodimers. Transient expression in mouse cortical neurons caused aggregation of α-II(mut)/β-II and α-II(mut)/β-III spectrin heterodimers, disrupted ankyrin-G and voltage-gated sodium channel clustering at the axon initial segment, and elevated the action potential threshold.

biological.citation: Essential Role of Sptan1 in Cochlear Hair Cell Morphology and Function Via Focal Adhesion Signaling. (PMID: 34708331)
biological.summary: Hair cell-specific knockout of Sptan1 in mice caused rapid deafness, abnormal stereocilia and cuticular plate formation, and loss of hair cells from middle and apical cochlear turns during early postnatal stages. Sptan1 deficiency reduced cell spreading and induced abnormal focal adhesion and integrin signaling, identifying SPTAN1 as critical for auditory function via focal adhesion regulation.

biological.citation: Loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 and SPTBN4 cause early-onset hereditary myopathy. (PMID: 40842327)
biological.summary: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 (frameshift, nonsense, splice-site) were identified in 14 families with early childhood-onset distal myopathy, with muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration of the distal lower limb anterior compartment. Muscle biopsy revealed myopathic changes, and nonsense-mediated decay of SPTAN1 mRNA was confirmed in patient muscle tissue, extending the SPTAN1 phenotypic spectrum to include skeletal muscle disease.

biological.citation: A shear stress-responsive pathway in monocytes drives cardiopulmonary bypass-induced inflammation via spectrin/RAF1/store-operated calcium entry. (PMID: 41579376)
biological.summary: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in THP-1 monocytic cells identified SPTAN1 and RAF1 as novel effectors of hemodynamic (shear) stress. SPTAN1 and RAF1 were found to activate store-operated calcium entry under cardiopulmonary bypass conditions, leading to elevated IL-8 expression, defining a SPTAN1/RAF1/SOCE pathway in sterile inflammation.

biological.citation: Lactylated SPTAN1 Accelerates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Promoting NOTCH1/HES1 Activation and Immunosuppression. (PMID: 41243220)
biological.summary: HBV infection promotes lactylation of SPTAN1 at K1952 and K1957 (mediated by AARS1, reversed by HDAC1), disrupting cytoplasmic liquid-liquid phase separation and driving nuclear translocation of SPTAN1. In the nucleus, lactylated SPTAN1 interacts with CBFB to activate NOTCH1/HES1 signaling, promoting HCC cell proliferation and PGE2-mediated immunosuppression via COX2/mPGES1.

biological.citation: Reduced migration of MLH1 deficient colon cancer cells depends on SPTAN1. (PMID: 24456667)
biological.summary: siRNA knockdown of MLH1 in HeLa, HEK293, and MLH1-positive HCT116 cells decreased SPTAN1 mRNA levels, indicating co-regulation. Overexpression of SPTAN1 rescued migration in MLH1-deficient cells, while SPTAN1 knockdown reduced mobility in MLH1-proficient cells, demonstrating that SPTAN1 is required for normal cellular motility in colorectal cancer cell lines.

biological.citation: Loss of Function SPTAN1 Variants Result in Ataxia and Intellectual Disability. (PMID: 39988451)
biological.summary: Ectopic expression of SPTAN1 p.(Gln1448Pro) and p.(Asn1839del) variants in zebrafish showed reduced protein abundance and impaired axonal localization of Sptan1. The p.(Gln1448Pro) variant failed to restore voltage-gated sodium channel localization in sptan1-null axons, and supplementation with D-aspartate improved motility in sptan1-null zebrafish, suggesting a therapeutic avenue for α-II spectrin-associated motor dysfunction.

biological.citation: Spectrins: molecular organizers and targets of neurological disorders. (PMID: 36697767)
biological.summary: SPTAN1 is expressed ubiquitously in the mammalian nervous system and encodes αII-spectrin, which varies in subcellular localization and specialization across neuronal subtypes. Pathogenic variants in SPTAN1 cause neurological disorders, and mouse model studies have illuminated its roles in neuronal membrane organization, axon initial segment integrity, and myelination.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Suppression of dominant-negative SPTAN1 allele in patient-derived cell lines via antisense oligonucleotide therapy (C. Wang et al.)
biological.summary: Antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) designed to induce RNase-mediated cleavage of the pathogenic p.D2303_L2305dup SPTAN1 mRNA allele achieved significant knockdown of mutant SPTAN1 expression in patient-derived iPSCs and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells and neurons, as confirmed by qPCR. This variant causes dominant-negative aggregation of thermolabile α/β spectrin heterodimers in glutamatergic neurons, and ASO-mediated allele suppression is being explored as a therapeutic strategy for DEE5.
